records.literal_gloss: Gather yourselves together, and gather, nation not ashamed,

en.L: Gather yourselves together, yes, gather, \q O nation without shame,
en.B: Gather yourselves together, come together, \q you nation without shame,
en.R: Come together and gather in one place, \q you nation that has no shame.

pt.L: Reúnam-se, sim, reúnam-se, \q ó nação que não sente vergonha,
pt.B: Reúnam-se, juntem-se, \q nação que não sente vergonha,
pt.R: Juntem-se e reúnam-se num só lugar, \q povo que não tem vergonha.

decisions.choice: gather yourselves together: come together, perhaps "gather like stubble"
decisions.reason: The verb is used for gathering straw or stubble (Exodus 5:7, 12), and is related to the word for stubble. Doubling it gives urgency, and it may also hint at what the nation is: stubble, soon to be blown away like the chaff of verse 2. The sense of the call is plain: assemble, as for a fast or an assembly of repentance (Joel 2:15-16), before it is too late.

decisions.choice: nation without shame: a nation that feels no shame
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "long for" (Genesis 31:30; Psalm 84:3), which would give "a nation that is not desired" or "that has no longing". In later Hebrew and Aramaic a related word means "be pale" with shame, and that sense fits the call to humble themselves in verse 3.

decisions.choice: the nation: Judah
alternatives: the Philistines and the other nations named after
decisions.reason: The oracles against the nations begin in verse 4. The call here, and the call to seek the LORD in verse 3, are addressed to Judah, the people threatened in chapter 1, while there is still time. |

decisions.choice: without shame (L, B); that has no shame (R)
decisions.reason: The levels follow the meaning chosen in m2; the footnote gives the other. Readable ends the verse with a full stop and begins verse 2 with "Do it", to keep its sentences short. |

decisions.choice: nação que não sente vergonha (L, B); povo que não tem vergonha (R)
decisions.reason: The sense taken in m2 is said with a clause: Brazilian "sem-vergonha" is an everyday insult and would make the call sound like abuse rather than a warning. The call is plural, so Judah is addressed with "vocês" in verses 1-3.

source.text: בְּטֶ֨רֶם֙ לֶ֣דֶת חֹ֔ק כְּמֹ֖ץ עָ֣בַר י֑וֹם בְּטֶ֣רֶם׀לֹא־יָב֣וֹא עֲלֵיכֶ֗ם חֲרוֹן֙ אַף־יְהוָ֔ה בְּטֶ֨רֶם֙ לֹא־יָב֣וֹא עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם י֖וֹם אַף־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: before [the] decree gives birth (like chaff a day passes by), before there comes upon you [the] burning of [the] anger of Yahweh, before there comes upon you [the] day of [the] anger of Yahweh.

en.L: before the decree gives birth, \q like chaff the day passes by; \q before there comes upon you the burning anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q before there comes upon you the day of the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: before the decree takes effect \q and the day blows away like chaff, \q before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s fierce anger falls on you, \q before the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anger overtakes you.
en.R: Do it before what God has decided comes to pass, \q before your time blows away like chaff. \q Do it before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s fierce anger comes on you, \q before the day when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shows {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger.

pt.L: antes que o decreto dê à luz, \q como palha o dia passa; \q antes que venha sobre vocês o ardor da ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, \q antes que venha sobre vocês o dia da ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.B: antes que o decreto se cumpra \q e o dia se vá como palha levada pelo vento, \q antes que caia sobre vocês a ira ardente {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, \q antes que os alcance o dia da ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.R: Façam isso antes que aconteça o que Deus decidiu, \q antes que o tempo de vocês seja levado como palha pelo vento. \q Façam isso antes que a ira ardente {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} caia sobre vocês, \q antes que chegue o dia em que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} vai mostrar a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} ira.

decisions.choice: before the decree gives birth, like chaff the day passes by: before God's decision is carried out and the time runs out
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is hard and reads like a broken line. "Gives birth" pictures the decree of judgment bringing forth what it holds, as a pregnant woman gives birth. "Like chaff the day passes" seems to mean that the time left is being blown away as chaff is blown off the threshing floor. The ancient translations read the line in different ways, and some suggest small changes to the text; the sense of urgency is clear either way.

decisions.choice: the burning of the anger of the LORD: his fierce anger
decisions.reason: Anger in Hebrew is "heat of the nose", and "burning" makes it stronger still. The phrase is common (Jeremiah 4:8; Nahum 1:6). |

decisions.choice: three times "before": the call is urgent
decisions.reason: The verse repeats "before" three times, each time nearer to the day itself. The call to gather in verse 1 and to seek the LORD in verse 3 must be answered before the day comes. |

decisions.choice: takes effect (B); comes to pass (R); gives birth (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of birth. Balanced and Readable say what it means (m1). Readable names God as the one who decided, which the verse implies. |

source.text: בַּקְּשׁ֤וּ אֶת־יְהוָה֙ כָּל־עַנְוֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִשְׁפָּט֖וֹ פָּעָ֑לוּ בַּקְּשׁוּ־צֶ֨דֶק֙ בַּקְּשׁ֣וּ עֲנָוָ֔ה אוּלַי֙ תִּסָּ֣תְר֔וּ בְּי֖וֹם אַף־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Seek Yahweh, all [the] humble of the land who have done his justice; seek righteousness, seek humility; perhaps you will be hidden on [the] day of [the] anger of Yahweh.

en.L: Seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all you humble of the land, \q who have done {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} justice; \q seek righteousness, seek humility; \q perhaps you will be hidden \q on the day of the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all you humble people of the land, \q you who carry out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands. \q Seek righteousness; seek humility. \q It may be that you will find shelter \q on the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anger.
en.R: Turn to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all you humble people of the land, \q you who obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws. \q Try hard to do what is right and to be humble. \q Then perhaps you will be kept safe \q on the day when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shows {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger.

pt.L: Busquem {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, todos vocês, humildes da terra, \q que praticaram a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} justiça; \q busquem a retidão, busquem a humildade; \q talvez vocês sejam escondidos \q no dia da ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.B: Busquem {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, todos vocês, os humildes da terra, \q vocês que cumprem os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} mandamentos. \q Busquem a retidão; busquem a humildade. \q Pode ser que vocês encontrem abrigo \q no dia da ira {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.R: Voltem-se para {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, todos vocês, pessoas humildes da terra, \q vocês que obedecem às {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} leis. \q Esforcem-se para fazer o que é certo e para ser humildes. \q Então talvez vocês fiquem protegidos \q no dia em que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} mostrar a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} ira.

decisions.choice: the humble of the land: the lowly, who depend on God
decisions.reason: The word means the poor and lowly, and often those who, having no power of their own, look to God (Isaiah 11:4; Psalm 37:11; Amos 2:7). In 3:12 the LORD promises to leave in Jerusalem "a people humble and lowly". Jesus' blessing on the meek who will inherit the earth (Matthew 5:5) takes up Psalm 37:11. |

decisions.choice: who have done his justice: who keep his commands
decisions.reason: "His justice" is what he has decided is right, his rulings and laws (Jeremiah 5:4-5; 8:7). Those who do it live by his law. Even they are told to go on seeking. |

decisions.choice: perhaps you will be hidden: perhaps the LORD will shelter you
decisions.reason: "Perhaps" leaves the rescue in God's hands, as in Joel 2:14 ("Who knows? He may turn") and Amos 5:15. Being hidden means being kept safe in time of danger (Psalm 27:5). There is a play on the prophet's name, Zephaniah, which means "the LORD has hidden" or "the LORD protects". |

decisions.choice: righteousness (L, B); to do what is right (R); his commands (B), his laws (R)
decisions.reason: Righteousness here is right living as God requires. Readable says "what is right", as the Amos table does. Balanced and Readable say "commands" and "laws" for "his justice" (m2). Readable says "Turn to" for "Seek", as elsewhere in the prophets. |

decisions.choice: a retidão (L, B), o que é certo (R); talvez (L, R), Pode ser que (B)
decisions.reason: Tsedeq is "retidão", as the Twelve set it beside mishpat "justiça"; Readable says "o que é certo", as the English does. "Talvez" and "Pode ser que" leave the rescue in God's hands (m3), as Amos 5:15 says it in Portuguese at each level. The play on Zephaniah's name, "the LORD has hidden", is left to the meaning note.

source.text: כִּ֤י עַזָּה֙ עֲזוּבָ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ה וְאַשְׁקְל֖וֹן לִשְׁמָמָ֑ה אַשְׁדּ֗וֹד בַּֽצָּהֳרַ֨יִם֙ יְגָ֣רְשׁ֔וּהָ וְעֶקְר֖וֹן תֵּעָקֵֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For Gaza will be abandoned, and Ashkelon [will become] a desolation; Ashdod, at noon they will drive her out, and Ekron will be uprooted.

en.L: For Gaza will be abandoned, \q and Ashkelon [will become] a desolation; \q Ashdod they will drive out at noon, \q and Ekron will be uprooted.
en.B: For Gaza will be deserted \q and Ashkelon left in ruins; \q Ashdod's people will be driven out at noon, \q and Ekron will be torn up by the roots.
en.R: Gaza will be left empty, \q and Ashkelon will be destroyed. \q The people of Ashdod will be driven out in the middle of the day, \q and Ekron will be pulled up by its roots.

pt.L: Porque Gaza será abandonada, \q e Asquelom [se tornará] uma desolação; \q Asdode, ao meio-dia a expulsarão, \q e Ecrom será desarraigada.
pt.B: Gaza ficará deserta, \q e Asquelom, em ruínas; \q o povo de Asdode será expulso ao meio-dia, \q e Ecrom será arrancada pela raiz.
pt.R: Gaza vai ficar vazia, \q e Asquelom vai ser destruída. \q O povo de Asdode vai ser expulso no meio do dia, \q e Ecrom vai ser arrancada pela raiz.

decisions.choice: Gaza abandoned, Ekron uprooted: plays on the names
decisions.reason: In Hebrew, "Gaza" ('azzah) and "abandoned" ('azuvah) sound alike, and so do "Ekron" ('eqron) and "uprooted" (te'aqer). Each city's name foretells its fate. The play cannot be kept in translation.

decisions.choice: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron: four of the five cities of the Philistines
decisions.reason: The Philistines lived on the coastal plain west of Judah, in five chief cities (Joshua 13:3). Gath, the fifth, is missing here, as in Amos 1:6-8 and Jeremiah 25:20; it may have lost its importance by then. |

decisions.choice: at noon: suddenly, in broad daylight
decisions.reason: Armies usually attacked at dawn. An attack at noon, during the hot hour of rest, would come when no one expected it (Jeremiah 6:4; 15:8). It may also mean that the city falls in half a day.

decisions.choice: in the middle of the day (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "in the middle of the day" for "at noon". |

decisions.choice: Gaza, Asquelom, Asdode, Ecrom
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the Philistine cities (m2) keep the forms Isaiah, Jeremiah and Amos 1:6-8 give them in Portuguese. The plays on Gaza and Ekron (m1) cannot be kept.

source.text: ה֗וֹי יֹֽשְׁבֵ֛י חֶ֥בֶל הַיָּ֖ם גּ֣וֹי כְּרֵתִ֑ים דְּבַר־יְהוָ֣ה עֲלֵיכֶ֗ם כְּנַ֨עַן֙ אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֖יךְ מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe [to the] inhabitants of the region of the sea, [the] nation of [the] Cherethites! [The] word of Yahweh [is] against you, Canaan, land of [the] Philistines, and I will destroy you until there is no inhabitant.

en.L: Woe, inhabitants of the seacoast, nation of Cherethites! \q The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines; \q and I will destroy you until no inhabitant [is left].
en.B: Woe to you who live by the sea, you nation of Cherethites! \q The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines: \q I will destroy you until no one is left.
en.R: How terrible it will be for you who live along the sea, you Cherethites! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines: \q I will destroy you until no one is left.

pt.L: Ai, habitantes da costa do mar, nação dos queretitas! \q A palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} [está] contra vocês, Canaã, terra dos filisteus; \q e eu te destruirei até não [restar] habitante.
pt.B: Ai de vocês que moram junto ao mar, nação dos queretitas! \q A palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} é contra vocês, Canaã, terra dos filisteus: \q Eu te destruirei até não sobrar ninguém.
pt.R: Que desgraça vai cair sobre vocês que moram no litoral, vocês, queretitas! \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} falou contra vocês, Canaã, terra dos filisteus: \q Vou te destruir até não sobrar ninguém.

decisions.choice: the Cherethites: a people from Crete, part of the Philistines
decisions.reason: The Cherethites are named beside the Philistines in 1 Samuel 30:14 and Ezekiel 25:16, and David's bodyguard included Cherethites (2 Samuel 8:18). The name is generally linked with Crete, from which, with Caphtor, the Philistines came (Amos 9:7; Jeremiah 47:4). |

decisions.choice: Canaan, land of the Philistines: the coastal part of Canaan
decisions.reason: Canaan is the name of the whole land west of the Jordan. The Philistine coast was part of it (Joshua 13:3). Calling the Philistines "Canaan" may also recall that Canaan's people were to be driven out. |

decisions.choice: and I will destroy you: the LORD's own words
decisions.reason: After "the word of the LORD is against you", the LORD himself speaks. The word that is against them is the word that follows. |

decisions.choice: Woe (L), Woe to (B), How terrible it will be for (R)
decisions.reason: The cry follows the Isaiah table for hoy. Balanced and Readable put a colon before the LORD's words. |

decisions.choice: Ai (L), Ai de (B), Que desgraça vai cair sobre (R); os queretitas
decisions.reason: The cry hoy keeps the Portuguese Isaiah 1:4 sets at each level. The Cherethites (m1) are "queretitas", the form 1 Samuel 30:14, 2 Samuel 8:18 and Ezekiel 25:16 use in Portuguese.

decisions.choice: vocês ... te
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "against you" in the plural to the people and then "I will destroy you" in the singular to the land of Canaan; Portuguese keeps the shift, with "vocês" for the people and God's "tu" for the land, so the words that follow are heard as the LORD's own (m3).

source.text: וְֽהָיְתָ֞ה חֶ֣בֶל הַיָּ֗ם נְוֺ֛ת כְּרֹ֥ת רֹעִ֖ים וְגִדְר֥וֹת צֹֽאן׃

records.literal_gloss: And the region of the sea will become pastures, meadows of shepherds and folds of flocks.

en.L: And the seacoast will become pastures, meadows for shepherds and folds for flocks.
en.B: The land by the sea will become pastureland, with meadows for shepherds and pens for sheep.
en.R: The land by the sea will become grassland, with shepherds' camps and pens for sheep.

pt.L: E a costa do mar se tornará pastagens, prados de pastores e currais de rebanhos.
pt.B: A terra junto ao mar se tornará pastagem, com prados para os pastores e currais para as ovelhas.
pt.R: A terra junto ao mar vai virar campo de pasto, com acampamentos de pastores e currais para as ovelhas.

decisions.choice: meadows: open grazing ground, or perhaps shepherds' caves or wells
decisions.reason: The word is rare and its meaning uncertain. It may be related to the words for "dig", giving caves or wells, or to a word for a grassy field. It also sounds like the name of the Cherethites in verse 5: the land of the Cherethites becomes a land of shepherds' grounds.

decisions.choice: the crowded coast becomes grazing land
decisions.reason: The cities of the Philistines will be empty, and shepherds will graze their flocks where the towns stood. Verse 7 says whose flocks they will be. |

decisions.choice: shepherds' camps (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "camps" for the places where shepherds stay with their flocks, leaving the uncertain word general (m1).

source.text: וְהָ֣יָה חֶ֗בֶל לִשְׁאֵרִ֛ית בֵּ֥ית יְהוּדָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם יִרְע֑וּן בְּבָתֵּ֣י אַשְׁקְל֗וֹן בָּעֶ֨רֶב֙ יִרְבָּצ֔וּן כִּ֧י יִפְקְדֵ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם וְשָׁ֥ב שְׁבִיתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] region will belong to [the] remnant of [the] house of Judah; on them they will graze; in [the] houses of Ashkelon in the evening they will lie down; for Yahweh their God will visit them and restore their fortunes.

en.L: And the region will be for the remnant of the house of Judah; on them they will graze; \q in the houses of Ashkelon in the evening they will lie down; \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God will visit them and restore their fortunes.
en.B: The coast will belong to what is left of the house of Judah; there they will pasture their flocks. \q In the evening they will lie down in the houses of Ashkelon, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God will care for them and restore their fortunes.
en.R: The land by the sea will belong to the people of Judah who are left alive. They will feed their flocks there. \q In the evening they will rest in the houses of Ashkelon. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} their God will take care of them and make things good for them again.

pt.L: E a região será do remanescente da casa de Judá; sobre elas pastarão; \q nas casas de Asquelom, à tarde, se deitarão; \q porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus deles, os visitará e restaurará a sorte deles.
pt.B: A costa pertencerá ao remanescente da casa de Judá; ali eles apascentarão os seus rebanhos. \q À tarde eles se deitarão nas casas de Asquelom, \q pois {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus deles, cuidará deles e restaurará a sua sorte.
pt.R: A terra junto ao mar vai pertencer ao povo de Judá que sobreviver. Eles vão levar os seus rebanhos para pastar ali. \q À tarde vão descansar nas casas de Asquelom. \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus deles, vai cuidar deles e fazer a vida deles voltar a ser boa.

decisions.choice: the remnant of the house of Judah: those of Judah who survive the judgment
decisions.reason: The prophets speak of a remnant who come through the judgment and receive the promises (Isaiah 10:20-22; Micah 2:12). In Zephaniah they are the humble people of 2:3 and 3:12-13. |

decisions.choice: will visit them: will come to care for them
decisions.reason: The same verb that means "punish" in 1:8-9 here means to attend to someone for good, as when God "visited" his people in Egypt (Genesis 50:24; Exodus 4:31; Ruth 1:6). |

decisions.choice: restore their fortunes: give back what they lost
decisions.reason: The phrase, "turn the turning", is used of restoring a people's former prosperity (Job 42:10; Jeremiah 30:3) and of bringing back exiles. The Hebrew text has two spellings here, one read as "captivity" and the other as "fortunes"; both senses fit a promise to a remnant.

decisions.choice: restore their fortunes (L, B); make things good for them again (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase follows the Jeremiah table. "On them" (L) refers to the pastures of verse 6; Balanced and Readable say "there". |

decisions.choice: o remanescente (L, B), o povo de Judá que sobreviver (R); restaurar a sorte (L, B), fazer a vida ... voltar a ser boa (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "o remanescente" is the prophets' word in Portuguese (m1), kept at Balanced where the English says "what is left of", so that the term is heard again in 3:13. The restoration (m3) keeps the Portuguese of Jeremiah 30:3 at each level.

source.text: שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ חֶרְפַּ֣ת מוֹאָ֔ב וְגִדּוּפֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן אֲשֶׁ֤ר חֵֽרְפוּ֙ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י וַיַּגְדִּ֖ילוּ עַל־גְּבוּלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: I have heard [the] taunting of Moab and [the] revilings of [the] sons of Ammon, with which they have taunted my people and made [themselves] great against their territory.

en.L: I have heard the taunting of Moab \q and the revilings of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon, \q with which they taunted {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people \q and made themselves great against their territory.
en.B: I have heard the taunts of Moab \q and the insults of the Ammonites, \q how they mocked {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people \q and made boasts against their land.
en.R: I have heard the people of Moab and Ammon \q insult and mock {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q They have bragged that they would take their land.

pt.L: Ouvi o insulto de Moabe \q e as injúrias dos filhos de Amom, \q com que insultaram o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo \q e se engrandeceram contra o território dele.
pt.B: Ouvi os insultos de Moabe \q e as ofensas dos amonitas, \q como zombaram do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo \q e se gabaram contra a terra dele.
pt.R: Ouvi o povo de Moabe e de Amom \q insultar e zombar do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo. \q Eles se gabaram de que iam tomar a terra dele.

decisions.choice: Moab and Ammon: Judah's neighbors east of the Jordan and the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Moab and Ammon were related to Israel through Lot, Abraham's nephew (Genesis 19:36-38), but were often its enemies. The prophets condemn their cruelty and pride (Amos 1:13-2:3; Isaiah 15-16; Jeremiah 48:1-49:6; Ezekiel 25:1-11). Ezekiel 25:3, 6 says that Ammon rejoiced when the temple was ruined and Judah went into exile. |

decisions.choice: made themselves great against their territory: boasted against Judah's land, or took part of it
alternatives: enlarged their own borders at Judah's expense
decisions.reason: The verb means "make great", and with "against" it means to boast or act arrogantly against someone (Jeremiah 48:26; Ezekiel 35:13). With "their territory" it may also mean that they seized land, as Ammon did in Gilead (Amos 1:13).

decisions.choice: the children of Ammon (L, gender default), the Ammonites (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal follows Jeremiah 49:1 with the gender setting, since the people of Ammon, men and women, are meant. Balanced and Readable use the name of the people. |

decisions.choice: os filhos de Amom (L), with no gender setting; os amonitas (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Jeremiah 49:1 has it in Portuguese, "filhos" already includes daughters, so the English gender span has no second Portuguese wording here or in verse 9. Moab and Ammon keep the forms Isaiah and Jeremiah give them.

source.text: לָכֵ֣ן חַי־אָ֡נִי נְאֻם֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כִּֽי־מוֹאָ֞ב כִּסְדֹ֤ם תִּֽהְיֶה֙ וּבְנֵ֤י עַמּוֹן֙ כַּֽעֲמֹרָ֔ה מִמְשַׁ֥ק חָר֛וּל וּמִכְרֵה־מֶ֥לַח וּשְׁמָמָ֖ה עַד־עוֹלָ֑ם שְׁאֵרִ֤ית עַמִּי֙ יְבָזּ֔וּם וְיֶ֥תֶר גּוֹיִ֖י יִנְחָלֽוּם׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore, [as] I live, declaration of Yahweh of hosts, God of Israel, surely Moab will be like Sodom and [the] sons of Ammon like Gomorrah, a place possessed by weeds and a pit of salt and a desolation forever; [the] remnant of my people will plunder them, and [the] rest of my nation will possess them.

en.L: Therefore, as I live, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel, Moab will surely be like Sodom and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon like Gomorrah, \q a place possessed by weeds, and a pit of salt, and a desolation forever; \q the remnant of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will plunder them, \q and the rest of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} nation will possess them.
en.B: Therefore, as I live, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, Moab will become like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah, \q a land overrun by weeds, a pit of salt, a wasteland forever. \q What is left of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will plunder them; \q the survivors of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} nation will take their land.
en.R: So, as surely as I live, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, Moab and Ammon will be destroyed like Sodom and Gomorrah. \q Their land will be covered with weeds and salt pits, and it will stay empty forever. \q Those of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people who are left will take their goods, \q and the survivors of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} nation will take over their land.

pt.L: Portanto, [tão certo como] eu vivo, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel, certamente Moabe será como Sodoma, e os filhos de Amom, como Gomorra, \q um lugar tomado por urtigas, e uma cova de sal, e uma desolação para sempre; \q o remanescente do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo os saqueará, \q e o restante da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} nação os possuirá.
pt.B: Portanto, tão certo como eu vivo, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel, Moabe se tornará como Sodoma, e os amonitas, como Gomorra, \q uma terra tomada pelo mato, um poço de sal, uma desolação para sempre. \q O que restar do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo os saqueará; \q os sobreviventes da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} nação tomarão a terra deles.
pt.R: Por isso, tão certo como eu vivo, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel, Moabe e Amom vão ser destruídos como Sodoma e Gomorra. \q A terra deles vai ficar coberta de mato e de poços de sal, e vai ficar vazia para sempre. \q Os do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo que sobrarem vão levar os bens deles, \q e os sobreviventes da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} nação vão ficar com a terra deles.

decisions.choice: as I live: the LORD swears by his own life
decisions.reason: People swore "as the LORD lives". The LORD, who has no one greater to swear by, swears by his own life (Numbers 14:21; Jeremiah 46:18; Ezekiel 33:11). It makes what follows certain. |

decisions.choice: like Sodom and like Gomorrah: destroyed and never rebuilt
decisions.reason: Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed by fire from the LORD (Genesis 19:24-28) and became the pattern of total destruction (Isaiah 1:9; 13:19; Amos 4:11). Moab and Ammon were born to Lot's daughters after the fall of Sodom (Genesis 19:30-38), so their end recalls their beginning. The salt pits fit the region by the Dead Sea, where the cities were thought to lie. |

decisions.choice: a place possessed by weeds: land taken over by nettles or thorny weeds
decisions.reason: The word for the weed is rare (Job 30:7; Proverbs 24:31); it is some plant that grows on neglected ground, perhaps nettles or chickweed. The land once possessed by Moab and Ammon will be possessed by weeds. |

decisions.choice: as I live, declares the LORD of hosts (L), of Armies (B); as surely as I live, says (R)
decisions.reason: The oath follows Jeremiah 46:18 at each level, and "the LORD of hosts" follows the Isaiah table. Readable joins Moab and Ammon in one clause and says "salt pits" for "a pit of salt". |

decisions.choice: [Tão certo como] eu vivo (L); Tão certo como eu vivo (B, R); o SENHOR dos Exércitos (every level)
decisions.reason: The LORD's oath by his own life (m1) keeps the Portuguese of Jeremiah 46:18 at each level, and YHWH Tsevaot is "o SENHOR dos Exércitos" at every level, where the English Balanced says "of Armies".

source.text: זֹ֥את לָהֶ֖ם תַּ֣חַת גְּאוֹנָ֑ם כִּ֤י חֵֽרְפוּ֙ וַיַּגְדִּ֔לוּ עַל־עַ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: This [will be] theirs in place of their pride, because they taunted and made [themselves] great against [the] people of Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: This [will be] theirs in return for their pride, \q because they taunted and boasted \q against the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: This is what they will get for their pride, \q because they mocked and boasted \q against the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: This will happen to them because they are proud. \q They insulted and bragged \q against the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

pt.L: Isto [será] deles em troca do seu orgulho, \q porque insultaram e se engrandeceram \q contra o povo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} dos Exércitos.
pt.B: É isto que receberão pelo seu orgulho, \q porque zombaram e se gabaram \q contra o povo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} dos Exércitos.
pt.R: Isso vai acontecer com eles porque são orgulhosos. \q Eles insultaram e se gabaram \q contra o povo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} dos Exércitos.

decisions.choice: their pride: the arrogance of Moab and Ammon
decisions.reason: Moab's pride was well known (Isaiah 16:6; Jeremiah 48:29). The punishment answers the sin: those who made themselves great will be brought low. |

decisions.choice: the people of the LORD of hosts: the prophet now speaks of the LORD in the third person
decisions.reason: In verses 8-9 the LORD speaks ("my people"). In verses 10-11 the prophet speaks about him. Such changes of speaker are common in the prophets. |

source.text: נוֹרָ֤א יְהוָה֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֣י רָזָ֔ה אֵ֖ת כָּל־אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיִשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ־לוֹ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִמְּקוֹמ֔וֹ כֹּ֖ל אִיֵּ֥י הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Fearsome [will be] Yahweh against them, for he will make lean all [the] gods of the earth; and they will bow down to him, each from his place, all [the] coastlands of the nations.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [will be] fearsome against them, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will starve \q all the gods of the earth; \q and they will bow down to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, each from its place, \q all the coastlands of the nations.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will be fearsome to them \q when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes all the gods of the earth waste away. \q Then they will bow down to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, each in its own place, \q all the coastlands of the nations.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will fill them with fear \q when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} takes away the power of all the gods of the earth. \q Then people from every nation, even lands far away, \q will worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, each in their own country.

pt.L: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} [será] temível contra eles, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fará definhar \q todos os deuses da terra; \q e se prostrarão diante {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, cada uma do seu lugar, \q todas as terras costeiras das nações.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} será temível para eles, \q quando fizer definhar todos os deuses da terra. \q Então se prostrarão diante {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, cada uma no seu lugar, \q todas as terras costeiras das nações.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} vai enchê-los de medo \q quando tirar o poder de todos os deuses da terra. \q Então pessoas de todas as nações, até de terras distantes, \q vão adorá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}, cada uma no seu próprio país.

decisions.choice: make lean: make the gods waste away
decisions.reason: The verb means "make thin, waste away" (Isaiah 17:4). The gods of the nations shrink to nothing when their worshipers turn to the LORD and their offerings stop.

decisions.choice: they will bow down to him, each from its place: the nations will worship the LORD in their own lands
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the nations come to Zion to worship (Isaiah 2:2-3; Zechariah 14:16). Here they worship the LORD where they are, as in Malachi 1:11, where incense is offered to his name "in every place". |

decisions.choice: the coastlands of the nations: the far-off lands along the sea
decisions.reason: The word means coasts and islands, and stands for the most distant lands known, to the west across the sea (Isaiah 41:1; Jeremiah 2:10). |

decisions.choice: coastlands (L, B), lands far away (R); fearsome (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Coastlands" follows the Isaiah table, with "lands far away" at Readable. The word for "fearsome" means "to be feared". Readable says "takes away the power of" for "makes waste away" (m1), and makes "each" plain as "each in their own country". |

decisions.choice: fará definhar (L, B); terras costeiras (L, B), terras distantes (R)
decisions.reason: The coastlands (m3) keep the words of Isaiah 41:1 in Portuguese at each level. "Definhar" is to waste away, the sense of the verb (m1).

records.literal_gloss: Also you, Cushites: slain of my sword [are] they.

en.L: You too, Cushites, \q slain by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword [are] they.
en.B: You too, Cushites, \q will be slain by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword.
en.R: You people of Cush, south of Egypt, \q will also be killed by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword.

pt.L: Também vocês, cuxitas, \q mortos pela {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} espada [são] eles.
pt.B: Também vocês, cuxitas, \q serão mortos pela {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} espada.
pt.R: Vocês, povo de Cuxe, ao sul do Egito, \q também vão ser mortos pela {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} espada.

decisions.choice: the Cushites: the people of Nubia, south of Egypt
decisions.reason: Cush lay along the Nile south of Egypt. For about fifty years before Zephaniah's time, until the Assyrians drove them out of Egypt in the 660s BC, kings from Cush ruled Egypt, so the name may stand for Egypt as well. Cush is the farthest land to the south, as Assyria (verse 13) is to the north. |

decisions.choice: you ... they: a sudden change of person
decisions.reason: The verse begins by addressing the Cushites and ends speaking of them. Such shifts are common in Hebrew poetry. The meaning is the same. |

decisions.choice: slain by my sword: killed in the LORD's judgment
decisions.reason: The LORD's sword is his judgment in battle (Isaiah 34:5-6; Jeremiah 46:10). The Cushites will fall in war, and it will be his doing. |

decisions.choice: will be slain (B), will be killed (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the address to the Cushites throughout (m2). Readable adds where Cush was. |

decisions.choice: cuxitas (L, B); povo de Cuxe (R)
decisions.reason: Cush and its people (m1) are "Cuxe" and "cuxitas", as Amos 9:7 and Isaiah have them in Portuguese; "etíopes" would point to modern Ethiopia.

source.text: וְיֵ֤ט יָדוֹ֙ עַל־צָפ֔וֹן וִֽיאַבֵּ֖ד אֶת־אַשּׁ֑וּר וְיָשֵׂ֤ם אֶת־נִֽינְוֵה֙ לִשְׁמָמָ֔ה צִיָּ֖ה כַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will stretch out his hand against [the] north and destroy Assyria, and he will make Nineveh a desolation, dry like the wilderness.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will stretch out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand against the north, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will destroy Assyria, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make Nineveh a desolation, \q dry like the wilderness.
en.B: He will raise {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand against the north \q and destroy Assyria; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will turn Nineveh into a wasteland, \q as dry as the desert.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will use {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power against the north \q and destroy Assyria. \q He will turn Nineveh into a ruin, \q as dry as a desert.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estenderá a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão contra o norte, \q e destruirá a Assíria, \q e fará de Nínive uma desolação, \q seca como o deserto.
pt.B: Ele levantará a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão contra o norte \q e destruirá a Assíria; \q fará de Nínive um lugar devastado, \q seco como o deserto.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} vai usar o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} poder contra o norte \q e destruir a Assíria. \q Ele vai transformar Nínive numa ruína, \q seca como um deserto.

decisions.choice: Assyria and Nineveh: the empire that ruled the region, and its capital
decisions.reason: Assyria had dominated Judah for a century. Nineveh, its capital on the Tigris, was taken and destroyed by the Babylonians and the Medes in 612 BC. Zephaniah speaks while it still stands; Nahum also foretells its fall. |

decisions.choice: the north: the direction from which Assyria's armies came
decisions.reason: Assyria lay to the north-east, but armies from Mesopotamia came into Judah from the north, along the fertile land, so the north stands for Assyria. |

decisions.choice: he will stretch out his hand: what the LORD will do, or a prayer that he may do it
alternatives: may he stretch out his hand
decisions.reason: The form of the verbs can be read as a statement or as a wish. Most read it as a statement, which matches verse 4 and 1:4.

decisions.choice: raise his hand (B); The LORD will use his power (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "raise his hand", the gesture of a blow. Readable names the LORD as the subject, which the verse implies, and says "use his power" for "stretch out his hand" (as at 1:4). |

source.text: וְרָבְצ֨וּ בְתוֹכָ֤הּ עֲדָרִים֙ כָּל־חַיְתוֹ־ג֔וֹי גַּם־קָאַת֙ גַּם־קִפֹּ֔ד בְּכַפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ יָלִ֑ינוּ ק֠וֹל יְשׁוֹרֵ֤ר בַּֽחַלּוֹן֙ חֹ֣רֶב בַּסַּ֔ף כִּ֥י אַרְזָ֖ה עֵרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And herds will lie down in her midst, every beast of a nation; both [the] desert owl and [the] hedgehog will lodge in her capitals; a voice will sing in the window, desolation [will be] on the threshold, for he has laid bare the cedar-work.

en.L: And herds will lie down in her midst, every beast of the nations; \q both the desert owl and the hedgehog \q will lodge on her capitals; \q a voice will sing in the window, desolation [will be] on the threshold, \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has laid bare the cedar work.
en.B: Flocks will lie down in her, animals of every kind; \q the desert owl and the hedgehog \q will roost on the tops of her pillars. \q Their call will sound through the windows, rubble will lie on the doorsteps, \q for her cedar paneling has been stripped bare.
en.R: Herds of animals of every kind will lie down there. \q Desert owls and hedgehogs \q will sleep on top of the broken columns. \q Birds will call from the windows, and the doorways will be full of rubble. \q The cedar wood on the walls will be torn away.

pt.L: E rebanhos se deitarão no meio dela, todo animal das nações; \q tanto a coruja do deserto como o ouriço \q pernoitarão nos seus capitéis; \q uma voz cantará na janela, desolação [haverá] na soleira, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} desnudou o madeiramento de cedro.
pt.B: Rebanhos se deitarão nela, animais de toda espécie; \q a coruja do deserto e o ouriço \q passarão a noite no alto das suas colunas. \q O seu canto soará pelas janelas, haverá entulho nas soleiras, \q pois os seus painéis de cedro foram arrancados.
pt.R: Rebanhos de animais de todo tipo vão se deitar ali. \q Corujas do deserto e ouriços \q vão dormir no alto das colunas quebradas. \q Aves vão cantar nas janelas, e as entradas vão ficar cheias de entulho. \q A madeira de cedro das paredes vai ser arrancada.

decisions.choice: every beast of the nations: animals of every kind
alternatives: every wild animal of the field
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual. It seems to mean all kinds of animals, as a nation is a kind of people. Some suggest a small change to read "every wild animal of the field".

decisions.choice: the desert owl and the hedgehog: creatures of ruins
decisions.reason: The same pair of creatures possesses ruined Edom in Isaiah 34:11, and the hedgehog ruined Babylon in Isaiah 14:23. The exact animals are uncertain; the second may be a kind of owl, which would fit their lodging on the pillars.

decisions.choice: desolation on the threshold: rubble lies in the doorways
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means "desolation" or "dryness". The Greek and Latin translations are generally said to read "ravens" (Hebrew 'orev for chorev, a difference of one letter), which would give a bird for the threshold to match the owl on the pillars and the voice in the window. The Hebrew text makes good sense, and is kept.

decisions.choice: capitals, cedar work: the remains of fine buildings
decisions.reason: The capitals are the carved tops of columns, now lying among the ruins or still standing. Cedar was used to panel palaces and temples (1 Kings 7:2-7; Jeremiah 22:14). When the roofs fall and the cedar is stripped, only the bare stone is left. "He" who laid it bare is the LORD, or the enemy he sends. |

decisions.choice: her cedar paneling has been stripped bare (B); will be torn away (R)
alternatives: he has laid bare the cedar work
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave the doer unnamed, because the verse does not say whether he is the LORD or the enemy (m4). Readable says "Birds will call" for "a voice will sing", which the line implies. |

decisions.choice: a coruja do deserto e o ouriço
decisions.reason: The creatures of ruins (m2) keep the names Isaiah 34:11 gives the same pair in Portuguese.

source.text: זֹ֞֠אתהָעִ֤יר הָעַלִּיזָה֙ הַיּוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת לָבֶ֔טַח הָאֹֽמְרָה֙ בִּלְבָבָ֔הּ אֲנִ֖י וְאַפְסִ֣י ע֑וֹד אֵ֣יךְ׀הָיְתָ֣ה לְשַׁמָּ֗ה מַרְבֵּץ֙ לַֽחַיָּ֔ה כֹּ֚ל עוֹבֵ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ יִשְׁרֹ֖ק יָנִ֥יעַ יָדֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: This [is] the exultant city that dwelt in security, that said in her heart, I [am], and there is none besides me still. How she has become a desolation, a lair for beasts! Everyone passing by her will hiss, will shake his hand.

en.L: This [is] the exultant city \q that dwelt in security, \q that said in her heart, "I [am], and there is none but me still." \q How she has become a desolation, a lair for wild animals! \q Everyone who passes by her \q will hiss and shake {{gender:their|his}} hand.
en.B: This is the city that exulted, \q that lived without a care, \q that thought in her heart, "I am, and there is no other but me." \q What a ruin she has become, a place where wild animals lie down! \q Everyone who passes by her \q hisses and shakes {{gender:their|his}} fist.
en.R: This is the proud city that felt so safe. \q It told itself, "I am the one, and there is no one else." \q But now look! It has become a ruin where wild animals rest. \q All who pass by will make fun of it \q and shake their fists at it.

pt.L: Esta [é] a cidade exultante \q que habitava em segurança, \q que dizia no seu coração: "Eu [sou], e não há outra além de mim." \q Como se tornou uma desolação, um covil de animais selvagens! \q Todo aquele que passa por ela \q assobiará e sacudirá a mão.
pt.B: Esta é a cidade que vivia em festa, \q que vivia despreocupada, \q que pensava no seu coração: "Eu sou, e não há outra além de mim." \q Que ruína ela se tornou, um lugar onde os animais selvagens se deitam! \q Todo aquele que passa por ela \q assobia e sacode o punho.
pt.R: Esta é a cidade orgulhosa que se sentia tão segura. \q Ela dizia a si mesma: "Eu sou a única, e não existe outra." \q Mas agora vejam! Ela virou uma ruína onde os animais selvagens descansam. \q Todos os que passam por ela vão zombar dela \q e sacudir os punhos contra ela.

decisions.choice: I am, and there is none but me: the words of Babylon in Isaiah 47:8, 10
decisions.reason: Isaiah 47:8 and 10 put the same words in the mouth of Babylon, the proud city that thought it could never fall. They are words that belong to God alone (Isaiah 45:5-6, 18), so the city claims for itself what is God's. Nineveh, which said them first, falls before Babylon does. |

decisions.choice: hiss and shake the hand: gestures of scorn and horror at a ruin
decisions.reason: Passers-by hiss or whistle and shake their hands at a ruined city, in horror and in mockery (Jeremiah 19:8; 49:17; Lamentations 2:15). |

decisions.choice: this is the exultant city: a taunt over the fallen city
decisions.reason: The verse is spoken as if Nineveh had already fallen, a mocking lament over a city that boasted of its safety. |

decisions.choice: I [am], and there is none but me still (L); I am, and there is no other but me (B); I am the one, and there is no one else (R)
decisions.reason: Where Zephaniah uses the words of Isaiah 47:8, each level uses the wording already published there. The gender setting gives "their" for the passer-by, man or woman; Readable makes the passers-by plural. Readable says "make fun of it" for "hiss", as Jeremiah 19:8 does. |

decisions.choice: the Portuguese of Isaiah 47:8 at each level
decisions.reason: The city's boast repeats Babylon's in Isaiah 47:8 and 10 (m1), so each level keeps Isaiah's Portuguese, feminine for the city: "Eu [sou], e não há outra além de mim" (L, B), "Eu sou a única, e não existe outra" (R).

decisions.choice: Todo aquele que ... a mão (L), o punho (B), with no gender setting
decisions.reason: "Todo aquele que" already means anyone, and Portuguese says "a mão" without a possessive, so the English gender span on "their/his" has no Portuguese counterpart.
